title: Ligaments of the pelvis and sacroiliac joint (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Attachments
Posterior ilium, lateral sacrum and coccyx to the ischial tuberosity.
Function
With the sacrospinous ligament it turns the sciatic notches into foramina and resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum under the weight of the trunk.
Attachments
Lateral margin of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine.
Function
Turns the greater sciatic notch into the greater sciatic foramen and separates it from the lesser sciatic foramen. It resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum.
hy: The pudendal nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine and this ligament, and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen.

rows: Attachments
Back of the sacrum to the posterior superior iliac spine and the adjacent ilium.
Function
With the interosseous sacroiliac ligament it carries the weight of the trunk from the sacrum to the hip bones.
Attachments
Transverse process of L5 to the posterior part of the iliac crest.
Function
Anchors L5 to the pelvis and keeps it from sliding forward on the sacrum.
Attachments
Ischial part of the rim of the acetabulum, spiraling over the back of the femoral neck to the base of the greater trochanter.
Function
Limits medial rotation and extension of the hip.
Attachments
Margins of the obturator foramen, closing it except for the obturator canal at the top.
Function
Gives origin to obturator internus and obturator externus. The obturator nerve and vessels leave the pelvis through the obturator canal.
Attachments
Tips of the spinous processes from C7 to the sacrum. Above C7 it continues as the ligamentum nuchae.
Function
Limits flexion of the vertebral column.
hy: The first ligament the needle passes in a midline lumbar puncture: supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura mater, arachnoid mater.
